bull_bear.body:
- Strong customer acceptance for flagship brands (Coastal, Coastal Premium, Coastal Gold, Jewel, President) across major international markets
- Modern seafood processing facilities and internationally recognised quality and food safety standards
- Established customer relationships across key international markets
- Diversified business portfolio (seafood exports plus renewable energy/biofuels via Coastal Biotech) reducing dependence on a single business and enhancing resilience
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- US reciprocal tariffs / trade policy risk — The global seafood industry, and the Company, faced reciprocal tariffs imposed by the United States during the year, resulting in additional costs; although tariffs were later reduced to 10% with an expected refund, the Company's exports remain exposed to changes in US trade policy.
- Geopolitical uncertainty — Continued geopolitical uncertainties were flagged as a principal challenge affecting the global seafood industry's operating environment during the year.
- Volatility in international demand — Volatile international demand and general volatility in demand and currency markets were cited among the principal challenges and threats facing the business.
- Competition from low-cost exporting nations — Intense competition from major exporting nations, including continued competition from Ecuador and other low-cost producing countries, pressures India's export competitiveness.
- Foreign exchange fluctuation risk — Foreign exchange fluctuations were flagged as a principal challenge; evidenced by a subsidiary (Continental Fisheries) reporting a marginal loss due to FX fluctuations on export financing facilities.
- Elevated financing costs following withdrawal of interest subvention — The withdrawal of interest subvention has raised financing costs for the industry and the Company.
- Aquaculture disease outbreaks and climate-related risk — The business remains exposed to disease outbreaks in aquaculture and climate-related risks, which can disrupt raw material (shrimp) supply.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company is engaged in processing and export of sea food, with a diversified portfolio of raw, cooked, IQF, butterfly, peeled, breaded, skewered, ready-to-cook, and value-added shrimp products, including premium Vannamei and Black Tiger shrimp, sold under its own flagship brands to customers across major international markets. Through its wholly owned subsidiary Coastal Biotech Private Limited, the Group has also diversified into ethanol/biofuel production, adding a revenue stream beyond seafood exports.

- **Ethanol/Biofuels:** ethanol

business.body:
- Strong customer acceptance for flagship brands (Coastal, Coastal Premium, Coastal Gold, Jewel, President) across major international markets
- Modern seafood processing facilities and internationally recognised quality and food safety standards
- Established customer relationships across key international markets
- Diversified business portfolio (seafood exports plus renewable energy/biofuels via Coastal Biotech) reducing dependence on a single business and enhancing resilience
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Diversified strategy focused on operational efficiency, cost optimization, market diversification, and product innovation in response to global trade challenges
- Strengthening presence in Europe, Japan, China, South Korea and other international markets while enhancing the value-added seafood product portfolio
- Diversification into renewable energy and biofuels through Coastal Biotech Private Limited, alongside the 3.6 MW captive solar power plant, to reduce dependence on the seafood business
- Expanding value-added seafood exports and strengthening presence in key international markets
- Improving operational efficiencies through technology and process optimization
- Maintaining the highest standards of quality, food safety, and regulatory compliance
- Promoting sustainability through responsible sourcing and energy-efficient operations
- Maintaining prudent financial discipline and delivering long-term value to shareholders
- The Company follows a voluntary Dividend Distribution Policy under which dividends (other than interim dividends) are declared at the AGM based on the Board's recommendation. Factors the Board considers before recommending a dividend include the Company's future expansion plans and capital requirements, profits earned during the fiscal year, cost of raising funds from alternate sources, liquidity position, applicable taxes, and general market conditions. The Company has not issued any GDRs/ADRs/warrants or convertible instruments, and no ESOPs were granted, vested or exercised during the year.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company's principal expansion during the year was the diversification into renewable energy and biofuels via wholly owned subsidiary Coastal Biotech Private Limited, whose ethanol plant completed its first full year of commercial operations in FY 2025-26, marking a major strategic milestone in diversifying the Group's revenue base beyond seafood exports. The Company also operates a 3.6 MW captive solar power plant supporting its sustainability initiatives. Management stated continuing investments in technology, quality assurance, renewable energy, and sustainable manufacturing practices to strengthen long-term competitiveness, but the text does not disclose any new named capex project with a commissioning/completion timeline for FY27.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Improving demand for value-added seafood products and expanding opportunities in international markets expected to support sustainable growth
- Expected contribution from Coastal Biotech Private Limited's ethanol business to enhance overall financial performance
- India's aquaculture and seafood sector offers strong long-term growth prospects, supported by favourable government policies, increasing global demand for high-quality seafood, and India's competitive advantage in aquaculture and seafood exports
- Rising global demand for value-added seafood products and ready-to-cook/convenience products in developed markets creating opportunities to improve product realization and operating margins
- The subsequent reduction of US reciprocal tariffs to 10% and an expected order for refund of tariffs already paid have significantly improved the industry outlook and strengthened confidence in future profitability
- Outlook remains positive barring any significant adverse developments in global market conditions, trade policies, or climatic factors
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers
